blocks.content: Soil pH directly controls the chemical availability of essential plant nutrients and the biological activity of soil microorganisms.

rows: Fungi tolerate and dominate in acidic pH
Bacteria and Actinomycetes thrive in neutral to alkaline pH

items: Gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) is used for sodic soil reclamation, whereas Agricultural Lime (CaCO3) is used for acid soil correction.
Phosphorus availability is severely reduced at low pH due to insoluble iron and aluminum phosphate formation, and at high pH due to calcium phosphate precipitation.
Soil buffering capacity refers to the inherent ability of a soil to resist rapid changes in its pH level.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Soil pH measures the negative logarithm of hydrogen ion concentration [H+] in the soil solution.
Most essential plant macronutrients (N, P, K, Ca, Mg, S) reach maximum availability at a neutral pH range of 6.5 to 7.5.
Acidic soils (pH < 6.5) are commonly neutralized using agricultural liming materials such as calcium carbonate.
Sodic and saline-alkaline soils (pH > 8.5) are reclaimed by applying gypsum followed by leaching with clean water.
Micronutrients like Iron, Manganese, Zinc, and Copper become toxic at extremely low pH and deficient at high pH.
